findings.issue_text: Double interpolation in runSplitQuery: queries are interpolated before execution and likely interpolated again downstream, causing variables whose values contain template syntax to be re-expanded

Emptiness filter (.filter on query.expr) runs before applyTemplateVariables, so queries whose variables resolve to empty strings pass the filter and flow into parsers with empty/mangled selectors, potentially throwing
Test mocks runQuery instead of exercising the real execution path, hiding whether real runQuery re-interpolates
Renaming interpolateVariablesInQueries to per-query applyTemplateVariables may drop array-level transformations like intervalMs/query type enrichment or refId ordering side effects

Repeated interpolation of the same target's expression per shard-group request in shardQuerySplitting.ts instead of interpolating once and reusing the result, which can produce incorrect expressions on later shards if template variable replacement is not idempotent

Potential double interpolation of the same query when runSplitQuery/runShardSplitQuery hand off to paths (e.g., runQuery) that also call applyTemplateVariables/interpolateVariablesInQueries downstream

Behavior change: old interpolateVariablesInQueries was called before the expr filter in runShardSplitQuery, so targets including hidden ones were mutated/normalized; new code filters first, which changes behavior for any code depending on those side effects

runSplitQuery now interpolates queries via datasource.applyTemplateVariables that the caller (LokiDatasource.query) likely already interpolated, causing double interpolation of variables whose output contains $ sequences, escaped variables, and $__auto ranges, silently producing different queries than authored
applyTemplateVariables does not interpolate step; the test only passes because the test mock's replace interpolates everything, so users with step: '$step' will send a literal '$step' to the backend

Per-query interpolation replaces batch interpolation, changing runShardSplitQuery call semantics from one interpolateVariablesInQueries call to 5 separate applyTemplateVariables calls, some receiving already-sharded queries with __stream_shard__ injected that applyTemplateVariables was never designed to see

Interpolation moved after hide/expr filtering in runShardSplitQuery, so hidden queries are no longer interpolated, losing side effects like variable dependency registration that affects variable load order and dashboard refresh scheduling

Double interpolation in shard-split path: applyTemplateVariables runs before splitQueriesByStreamShard, which likely also interpolates shard queries, causing ad-hoc filters or non-idempotent replacements (e.g. $__auto) to be applied twice and silently corrupt queries (shardQuerySplitting.ts:49-52)

Same double-interpolation risk in runSplitQuery: interpolated queries are passed to datasource.runQuery, which may re-interpolate via interpolateVariablesInQueries before sending to backend (querySplitting.ts:296-299)

applyTemplateVariables may mutate shared query objects in request.targets in place, losing the original un-interpolated query text for retries, re-splitting, caching, or error messages (shardQuerySplitting.ts:50, querySplitting.ts:298)

Mock implementations of applyTemplateVariables in shardQuerySplitting.test.ts:53-58 and 170-175 have arrow bodies with no return, so they return undefined instead of the query, causing tests to verify mutation side effects rather than the real API contract where the production code relies on the return value

New interpolation tests in querySplitting.test.ts:75-86 and shardQuerySplitting.test.ts:84-98 mock runQuery and only inspect the first call's arguments, so there's no integration coverage that interpolated queries survive the actual split/shard pipeline end-to-end, including that interpolation happens exactly once per request rather than being re-applied per chunk/shard

Tests don't verify that interpolated exprs are used for the splitting decisions themselves (querySupportsSplitting, isLogsQuery evaluated on interpolated queries), a behavioral change with no dedicated test for queries that only become logs/supported queries after interpolation

Behavioral change in filter/interpolate ordering in shardQuerySplitting.ts:48-53: previously interpolated first then filtered empty expr, now filters empty expr first then interpolates, so a query with a template variable that interpolates to an empty string is no longer dropped and flows into splitQueriesByStreamShard with an empty interpolated expr, with no test coverage for this edge case

Assertion at shardQuerySplitting.test.ts:112 changed to expect applyTemplateVariables called 5 times but only verifies the count, without asserting that each of the 5 shard queries received the interpolated expr or that shard-splitting logic operated on the interpolated selector

Double interpolation risk: runSplitQuery in querySplitting.ts:293-299 calls applyTemplateVariables but the real datasource runQuery may re-interpolate, corrupting escaped variables ($${var}) and query text
Tests cannot detect the double interpolation problem because runQuery is fully mocked, making the interpolation tests silent-pass
Same double-interpolation pattern in shardQuerySplitting.ts:49-53 where interpolated queries are passed to runQuery which may re-interpolate, mangling $ characters after the shard suffix is appended
Inconsistent mutation of request.targets: only visible non-empty queries are interpolated, so if applyTemplateVariables mutates in place, request.targets ends up partially mutated

Behavior change in shard splitting: filtering order changed from interpolate-all-then-filter to filter-then-interpolate, so hidden queries no longer get interpolated, with no test asserting hidden-query behavior
request.filters is now passed to applyTemplateVariables but DataQueryRequest.filters is optional/undefined on several code paths, potentially causing unguarded access errors in production

adjudication_records.issue_text: Double interpolation in runSplitQuery: queries are interpolated before execution and likely interpolated again downstream, causing variables whose values contain template syntax to be re-expanded

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `runSplitQuery` now applies `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...)` once when building `queries` (via `.map(...)`), and adds tests asserting the resulting `runQuery` call receives interpolated `expr`/`step`. There is no evidence in the shown diff that queries are interpolated again “downstream” (e.g., inside `runQuery` or later stages), so the claim of double interpolation cannot be verified from this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Emptiness filter (.filter on query.expr) runs before applyTemplateVariables, so queries whose variables resolve to empty strings pass the filter and flow into parsers with empty/mangled selectors, potentially throwing

adjudication.rationale: In both runSplitQuery() and runShardSplitQuery(), the pipeline filters on `query.expr` before calling `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...)` (e.g. `.filter((query) => query.expr) ... .map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...))`). This means a target with a non-empty templated expr (like `$var`) will pass the filter even if templating resolves it to an empty string, so subsequent logic will receive an interpolated query whose `expr` may now be empty. The diff does not show downstream parsers throwing on empty expr, so the claimed failure is plausible but not directly verifiable here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test mocks runQuery instead of exercising the real execution path, hiding whether real runQuery re-interpolates

adjudication.rationale: The new tests explicitly spy on and mock `datasource.runQuery` to assert that `runSplitQuery`/`runShardSplitQuery` pass already-interpolated targets (they check `mock.calls[0][0].targets[0]....`). That does not “hide” a defect in this diff: the change being tested is the new `.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...))` before calling `runQuery`. Whether the *real* `runQuery` also interpolates (potential double interpolation) is not shown anywhere in the diff, so the finding’s concern cannot be verified from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Renaming interpolateVariablesInQueries to per-query applyTemplateVariables may drop array-level transformations like intervalMs/query type enrichment or refId ordering side effects

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `interpolateVariablesInQueries` being replaced by per-query `applyTemplateVariables` in both `runSplitQuery` and `runShardSplitQuery`, with new tests asserting interpolation happens before execution. There is no evidence in the diff that `interpolateVariablesInQueries` performed any array-level transformations (e.g., `intervalMs`/type enrichment, refId ordering side effects); the prior tests mocked it only to do string replacement on `expr`. The finding is speculative and not verifiable from the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Repeated interpolation of the same target's expression per shard-group request in shardQuerySplitting.ts instead of interpolating once and reusing the result, which can produce incorrect expressions on later shards if template variable replacement is not idempotent

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `runShardSplitQuery` now interpolates via `.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...))` exactly once over the filtered `request.targets` (see `shardQuerySplitting.ts`), not per shard-group request. The finding claims repeated interpolation in `shardQuerySplitting.ts`, but that behavior is not shown in this diff. Any additional calls (e.g., the test expecting `applyTemplateVariables` to be called 5 times) would have to come from `splitQueriesByStreamShard`, which is not part of the provided diff and cannot be attributed to `shardQuerySplitting.ts` here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Potential double interpolation of the same query when runSplitQuery/runShardSplitQuery hand off to paths (e.g., runQuery) that also call applyTemplateVariables/interpolateVariablesInQueries downstream

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that `runSplitQuery` and `runShardSplitQuery` now call `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...)` on each target before further processing, and tests assert the interpolated values are passed into `datasource.runQuery`. However, nothing in the provided diff shows that `runQuery` (or any downstream path invoked from these functions) also performs interpolation again. The claim of "double interpolation" depends on behavior outside this diff and is not verifiable from the changes shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Behavior change: old interpolateVariablesInQueries was called before the expr filter in runShardSplitQuery, so targets including hidden ones were mutated/normalized; new code filters first, which changes behavior for any code depending on those side effects

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a real behavior change in `runShardSplitQuery`: previously `datasource.interpolateVariablesInQueries(request.targets, ...)` was invoked on all targets (including hidden / expr-less) before `.filter(query => query.expr).filter(query => !query.hide)`. Now it filters first and only then calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...)` via `.map(...)`, so hidden or expr-less targets will no longer be interpolated/mutated. Whether any downstream code relies on those side effects isn’t proven in the diff, but the ordering/side-effect change itself is verifiable and could matter if interpolation mutates the original objects (as tests’ mock implementations do).

adjudication_records.issue_text: runSplitQuery now interpolates queries via datasource.applyTemplateVariables that the caller (LokiDatasource.query) likely already interpolated, causing double interpolation of variables whose output contains $ sequences, escaped variables, and $__auto ranges, silently producing different queries than authored

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `runSplitQuery` and `runShardSplitQuery` now calling `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...)` on each target before splitting/executing. However, the finding’s core claim—"the caller (LokiDatasource.query) likely already interpolated" leading to double interpolation—is not verifiable from this diff because no changes or context for `LokiDatasource.query` (or any existing interpolation there) are shown. The added tests actually assert that interpolation happens here, but do not demonstrate double interpolation or altered behavior from a second pass.

adjudication_records.issue_text: applyTemplateVariables does not interpolate step; the test only passes because the test mock's replace interpolates everything, so users with step: '$step' will send a literal '$step' to the backend

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `runSplitQuery`/`runShardSplitQuery` now call `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...)` on each target, and the newly added tests explicitly assert that `step: '$step'` becomes `'5m'` in the request passed to `runQuery`. The implementation of `applyTemplateVariables` itself is not shown in this diff, so the claim that it "does not interpolate step" cannot be verified from the provided changes, and it directly contradicts what the added tests are checking.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Per-query interpolation replaces batch interpolation, changing runShardSplitQuery call semantics from one interpolateVariablesInQueries call to 5 separate applyTemplateVariables calls, some receiving already-sharded queries with __stream_shard__ injected that applyTemplateVariables was never designed to see

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change interpolation semantics: `runShardSplitQuery` no longer calls a single `interpolateVariablesInQueries(...)` on the whole `targets` array, and instead applies `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...)` via `.map(...)` (and the test expectation is updated from 1 call to 5 calls). However, the claim that `applyTemplateVariables` is "never designed to see" already-sharded `__stream_shard__` queries is not verifiable from this diff alone (we can’t see `applyTemplateVariables`’s contract/implementation), so the concern is architectural/performance/semantics rather than a confirmed defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Interpolation moved after hide/expr filtering in runShardSplitQuery, so hidden queries are no longer interpolated, losing side effects like variable dependency registration that affects variable load order and dashboard refresh scheduling

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `runShardSplitQuery` from interpolating all `request.targets` first (`interpolateVariablesInQueries(request.targets, ...)`) to interpolating only after filtering out `!query.expr` and `query.hide` (`.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...))`), so hidden queries are indeed no longer interpolated. However, the claimed consequence—"losing side effects like variable dependency registration" affecting load order/refresh scheduling—is not shown or evidenced anywhere in this diff (neither `applyTemplateVariables` nor `interpolateVariablesInQueries` implementations are present), so that impact cannot be verified from the PR changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Double interpolation in shard-split path: applyTemplateVariables runs before splitQueriesByStreamShard, which likely also interpolates shard queries, causing ad-hoc filters or non-idempotent replacements (e.g. $__auto) to be applied twice and silently corrupt queries (shardQuerySplitting.ts:49-52)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `runShardSplitQuery` now applies `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...)` to each target before calling `splitQueriesByStreamShard` (shardQuerySplitting.ts). The updated test also expects `applyTemplateVariables` to have been called 5 times for a single request, implying additional calls likely happen deeper in the shard-splitting path. This makes the review concern about potential double interpolation / redundant interpolation plausible and diff-grounded, but the claim of actual query corruption cannot be conclusively verified from the provided diff because `splitQueriesByStreamShard`’s implementation is not shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Same double-interpolation risk in runSplitQuery: interpolated queries are passed to datasource.runQuery, which may re-interpolate via interpolateVariablesInQueries before sending to backend (querySplitting.ts:296-299)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows runSplitQuery now applies `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...)` to each target before splitting and then passes those targets to `datasource.runQuery`. However, the claim that `datasource.runQuery` "may re-interpolate via interpolateVariablesInQueries" is not evidenced anywhere in this diff: there is no change or reference showing `runQuery` performs additional interpolation, nor is `interpolateVariablesInQueries` invoked from runSplitQuery after this change. The finding relies on external/unstated behavior not verifiable from the provided diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: applyTemplateVariables may mutate shared query objects in request.targets in place, losing the original un-interpolated query text for retries, re-splitting, caching, or error messages (shardQuerySplitting.ts:50, querySplitting.ts:298)

adjudication.rationale: In both querySplitting.ts and shardQuerySplitting.ts the code now does `.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, ...))` directly on objects coming from `request.targets` after filtering. This passes the original query object references into `applyTemplateVariables`. The tests’ mocks for `applyTemplateVariables` explicitly mutate `query.expr` and return the same object, demonstrating that in-place mutation is possible with this call pattern. The diff doesn’t prove the real `applyTemplateVariables` mutates, nor that losing the un-interpolated text breaks behavior, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded side-effect risk (shared input objects can be mutated).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Mock implementations of applyTemplateVariables in shardQuerySplitting.test.ts:53-58 and 170-175 have arrow bodies with no return, so they return undefined instead of the query, causing tests to verify mutation side effects rather than the real API contract where the production code relies on the return value

adjudication.rationale: In shardQuerySplitting.test.ts, both shown mockImplementation bodies explicitly `return query;` (e.g., the blocks replacing interpolateVariablesInQueries now end with `return query;`). Therefore they do not return undefined, and the finding misreads the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New interpolation tests in querySplitting.test.ts:75-86 and shardQuerySplitting.test.ts:84-98 mock runQuery and only inspect the first call's arguments, so there's no integration coverage that interpolated queries survive the actual split/shard pipeline end-to-end, including that interpolation happens exactly once per request rather than being re-applied per chunk/shard

adjudication.rationale: The new tests (`querySplitting.test.ts` added block and `shardQuerySplitting.test.ts` added block) stub `datasource.runQuery` and then only assert against `jest.mocked(datasource.runQuery).mock.calls[0][0]...`, i.e., the first `runQuery` invocation’s first target. If `runSplitQuery`/`runShardSplitQuery` issues multiple `runQuery` calls (per chunk/shard), these tests don’t verify interpolation is preserved across all generated requests/targets, nor do they assert anything about how many times interpolation is applied. This is a test coverage/precision gap rather than a demonstrated functional defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Tests don't verify that interpolated exprs are used for the splitting decisions themselves (querySupportsSplitting, isLogsQuery evaluated on interpolated queries), a behavioral change with no dedicated test for queries that only become logs/supported queries after interpolation

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes behavior so splitting classification now happens on interpolated queries: in `runSplitQuery` targets are `.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...))` before `partition(...querySupportsSplitting)` and before `isLogsQuery(query.expr)`. The new tests only assert that the interpolated `expr`/`step` are passed to `runQuery`, not that `querySupportsSplitting` / `isLogsQuery` decisions are made on interpolated values (e.g., a query that becomes a logs query or becomes splittable only after interpolation). This is a specific, diff-grounded missing-test gap for newly introduced nontrivial logic, not a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Behavioral change in filter/interpolate ordering in shardQuerySplitting.ts:48-53: previously interpolated first then filtered empty expr, now filters empty expr first then interpolates, so a query with a template variable that interpolates to an empty string is no longer dropped and flows into splitQueriesByStreamShard with an empty interpolated expr, with no test coverage for this edge case

adjudication.rationale: In shardQuerySplitting.ts the pipeline changed from `interpolateVariablesInQueries(...).filter(query => query.expr)` to filtering on the *pre-interpolated* `query.expr` and only then `.map(query => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...))`. This means a target whose `expr` is non-empty before interpolation but becomes empty after `applyTemplateVariables` would now pass the filters and be forwarded to `splitQueriesByStreamShard` with an empty `expr`. The diff doesn’t show whether downstream code breaks, but the ordering change and the uncovered edge case are real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Assertion at shardQuerySplitting.test.ts:112 changed to expect applyTemplateVariables called 5 times but only verifies the count, without asserting that each of the 5 shard queries received the interpolated expr or that shard-splitting logic operated on the interpolated selector

adjudication.rationale: While the assertion in `shardQuerySplitting.test.ts` was changed to only check `applyTemplateVariables` call count, the diff also adds a new test (`Interpolates queries before execution`) that asserts the *executed* shard query expression contains interpolated values (`[5m]`, `step: '5m'`) and shard-splitting output (`__stream_shard__=~"20|10" ... drop __stream_shard__`). So the finding’s claim that the tests don’t assert interpolation/shard logic beyond a call count is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Double interpolation risk: runSplitQuery in querySplitting.ts:293-299 calls applyTemplateVariables but the real datasource runQuery may re-interpolate, corrupting escaped variables ($${var}) and query text

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows runSplitQuery/runShardSplitQuery now explicitly call datasource.applyTemplateVariables() before later invoking datasource.runQuery(), and tests were added to assert the interpolated expr/step passed into runQuery. The claim that the “real datasource runQuery may re-interpolate” (causing double interpolation/corruption of $${var}) is not evidenced anywhere in this diff: there is no change to runQuery, no indication runQuery performs interpolation, and no diff context demonstrating escaped-variable handling. The finding relies on behavior outside what’s shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Tests cannot detect the double interpolation problem because runQuery is fully mocked, making the interpolation tests silent-pass

adjudication.rationale: The new tests explicitly inspect the arguments passed to the mocked `datasource.runQuery` (e.g., `mock.calls[0][0].targets[0].expr` and `.step`) after running `runSplitQuery`/`runShardSplitQuery`, which directly verifies that template interpolation happened before execution. Mocking `runQuery` does not make these tests “silent-pass”; it enables capturing the call payload. The diff also shows interpolation is performed via `.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...))` before any `runQuery` call. A “double interpolation problem” is not evidenced in this diff, and the tests would still observe the final interpolated values passed to `runQuery`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Same double-interpolation pattern in shardQuerySplitting.ts:49-53 where interpolated queries are passed to runQuery which may re-interpolate, mangling $ characters after the shard suffix is appended

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows shardQuerySplitting.ts now applies template variables once via `.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...))` before splitting and running. There is no evidence in this diff that `runQuery` “re-interpolates” or that `$` characters get mangled after shard suffixing; `runQuery`’s behavior isn’t shown. The new/updated tests explicitly assert that `runQuery` receives already-interpolated `expr`/`step`, which contradicts the claim of a double-interpolation defect being present/introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent mutation of request.targets: only visible non-empty queries are interpolated, so if applyTemplateVariables mutates in place, request.targets ends up partially mutated

adjudication.rationale: Both runSplitQuery() and runShardSplitQuery() now do `.filter(...).map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, ...))` directly on query objects coming from `request.targets`. If `applyTemplateVariables` mutates the passed `query` in place (as the updated tests’ mocks do), then only the filtered subset (non-hidden + having `expr`) will be mutated, leaving the rest of `request.targets` untouched. The diff doesn’t show any immediate incorrect behavior, but it introduces a diff-grounded side-effect/consistency concern (partial mutation of the original request object) that could matter if `request.targets` is later reused/inspected elsewhere.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Behavior change in shard splitting: filtering order changed from interpolate-all-then-filter to filter-then-interpolate, so hidden queries no longer get interpolated, with no test asserting hidden-query behavior

adjudication.rationale: In `runShardSplitQuery` the pipeline changed from `datasource.interpolateVariablesInQueries(request.targets, ...)` followed by filtering (`expr`, `!hide`) to filtering first and then `.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...))`. This does mean hidden queries (and those without `expr`) will no longer be interpolated at all, which is a behavior change visible in the diff. The diff adds tests for interpolation-before-execution, but none assert whether hidden queries should/shouldn’t be interpolated, so the finding about an untested behavior change is grounded. It’s not clearly a correctness bug because hidden queries are not executed anyway.

adjudication_records.issue_text: request.filters is now passed to applyTemplateVariables but DataQueryRequest.filters is optional/undefined on several code paths, potentially causing unguarded access errors in production

adjudication.rationale: The diff only shows `request.filters` being forwarded as the third argument to `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...)` in both `runSplitQuery` and `runShardSplitQuery`. Passing a possibly-undefined value as an argument does not itself cause an error, and the diff does not show `applyTemplateVariables` accessing `filters` without guards or even its signature/implementation. Therefore the claim of “unguarded access errors in production” is not verifiable from this diff.
